subject: Parser hang: some completions missing final marker
body:
From: Ben Harper <b.harper@halohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Missing 'END_OF_DOC' marker in some completions — downstream parser hangs

Hey Jordan,

We're seeing a problem in production where ~3-6% of completions returned by Redwood are missing our final marker line (we use '--- END_OF_DOC ---' to know when a generation is complete). When that happens our parser waits indefinitely and the ingest pipeline stalls. We reproduced this both in staging and prod.

Sample prompt (truncated):
> Generate a one-paragraph summary for the clinical note below. Terminate with a final line exactly: --- END_OF_DOC ---

Observed outputs (two examples):
1) "The patient presented with...
--- END_OF_DOC ---"  (OK)
2) "The patient presented with..."  (NO MARKER, parser waits)

We collected some session exports and a short log of request IDs where the downstream consumer hung. Attaching session_export_101.jsonl and halo_staging_logs_20261019.txt. Please let us know if this is something on your side or ours — it is reproducible for us.

Thanks,
Ben Harper
Engineering Manager, HaloHealth
ben.harper@halohealth.com

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Harper <b.harper@halohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Missing 'END_OF_DOC' marker in some completions — downstream parser hangs

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear repro and the attachments. I've looped in our CS lead Marissa and infra engineer Marcus so we can triage. A few quick asks while we investigate: 

- Can you paste a couple of the request IDs and timestamps (UTC) from the logs — we'll look for matching delivery/stream events on our side.
- Which model and API version were you using for these requests?
- Do you see the same behavior when using non-streaming (complete response) vs streaming?

Temporary mitigation: if you can, please add a short post-process that appends the marker if absent — we know that's painful but will prevent the parser hang while we triage.

We'll prioritize this.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: initial triage for HaloHealth marker issue

Quick notes from my initial investigation: 

- I pulled the three request IDs Ben sent and traced them through our routing and serving logs. All three requests completed normally on the model side and the generation output that left our runtime includes the exact trailing string '--- END_OF_DOC ---' in the final chunk.
- Delivery logs (edge -> customer) show the SSE stream for the streaming request had normal chunking and final event termination for the calls we checked. For the non-streaming requests the HTTP response body contains the full text including the marker.
- No evidence of truncation or token-drop on our side for these sessions.

Hypothesis: their streaming consumer on the client side may be closing the socket early under a particular combination of network conditions and read-timeout handling, which would cause the parser to never observe the marker. I tried to reproduce a client-side truncation by simulating a slow reader and saw identical behavior when the client read loop times out before the final frame.

Recommended next steps: 
1) Ask customer to share the client library / runtime for their streaming consumer (language/runtime and timeout settings).
2) Recommend immediate mitigation: add an idempotent post-process to append '--- END_OF_DOC ---' if absent, increase read timeout on the consumer, and ensure the SSE client treats the final event as part of the stream rather than a separate connection close.
3) We can add extra logging to the edge layer for a short window to capture any abnormal FIN/RST events correlated to their IPs if they grant permission.

I'll prepare a short note to send back to Ben. No platform regression appears present based on the samples.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Harper <b.harper@halohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Missing 'END_OF_DOC' marker in some completions — downstream parser hangs

Hi Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround on the IDs and logs. Marcus dug into the session traces and we couldn't find any instance where the generated text left our stack without the trailing marker. Short summary:

- Evidence on our side: the model outputs and responses we sent include the exact final marker string for the requests you provided. The network/edge delivery logs show normal stream termination events.
- Most likely cause: the client-side streaming consumer is intermittently terminating the read loop prior to receiving the final frame under certain network/timeouts. Marcus was able to reproduce the hang by simulating a slow client-side reader.

Practical recommendations we suggest you try immediately:
1) Add a lightweight post-processor that, if the final line does not equal '--- END_OF_DOC ---', appends the marker so your parser can safely complete.
2) Increase your SSE/stream read timeouts by at least 1.5x and ensure the client treats the final event as a normal stream termination rather than ignoring a late chunk.
3) If you can share the exact SSE client/library version and connection settings we can look for known issues and recommend more specific configuration changes.

If you'd like we can also enable short-term packet-level logging for your IP block to capture any edge-level FIN/RST that might explain an unexpected connection close (we would need your OK to collect that).

If this aligns with what you see, we consider this a closure on the Redwood side — no platform regression found. We'll remain available to support your mitigation and can reopen if you identify evidence showing the marker was present on the wire but not in the client.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Ben Harper <b.harper@halohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Missing 'END_OF_DOC' marker in some completions — downstream parser hangs

Jordan / Marcus — thanks for the thorough investigation and the reproduction notes. We'll put the post-process in place and bump our read timeout. I'll follow up once we've validated in prod. We do not want to enable packet-level logging right now — I'll reach out if the problem persists after our mitigations.

Appreciate the quick help.
Ben

Attachments: session_export_101.jsonl (session exports), halo_staging_logs_20261019.txt (raw logs), screenshot_parser_hang.png (parser UI capture)
